strings.d1.theme: Union Square, Chinatown and cable cars
strings.d1.s0.name: Powell Street Cable Car
strings.d1.s0.tips: The Powell-Hyde line has run since 1873. Go at 08:30 to skip the queue, hang off the side and get off at Lombard.
strings.d1.s1.name: Lombard Street
strings.d1.s1.tips: The 'world's crookedest street' has 8 hairpin bends. Look down it from Hyde.
strings.d1.s2.name: Chinatown Dragon Gate & Grant Avenue
strings.d1.s2.tips: The oldest Chinatown in North America. Visit the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory (Ross Alley).
strings.d1.s3.name: Good Mong Kok Bakery
strings.d1.s3.tips: Cash-only boxes of dim sum, and the queue moves fast.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
strings.d1.s4.tips: A market in the 1898 ferry building: oysters (Hog Island), Blue Bottle, Acme sourdough, and a farmers' market on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays.
strings.d1.b0.name: Boudin Bakery Fisherman's Wharf
strings.d1.b0.tips: Sourdough since 1849. Try the clam chowder served in a bread bowl.
strings.d1.b1.name: Exploratorium
strings.d1.b1.tips: Science museum at Pier 15, an alternative to the Embarcadero.
strings.d2.theme: Golden Gate by bike and Sausalito
strings.d2.s0.name: Crissy Field & Fort Point
strings.d2.s0.tips: Rent a bike at Fisherman's Wharf (40 USD/day). Ride the Presidio shore to the bridge, passing the Palace of Fine Arts on the way.
strings.d2.s1.name: Golden Gate Bridge
strings.d2.s1.tips: Cycle the 2.7 km bridge (east pavement on weekdays). Expect fog until noon in summer, and wind.
strings.d2.s2.name: Sausalito
strings.d2.s2.tips: A Mediterranean feel just beyond the bridge, with houseboats at Waldo Point.
strings.d2.s3.name: Fish Sausalito
strings.d2.s3.tips: Sustainable seafood by the harbour. Cash only.
strings.d2.s4.name: Sausalito Ferry
strings.d2.s4.tips: Take the Golden Gate Ferry back to the city with your bike, with views of Alcatraz and the skyline.
strings.d2.b0.name: Golden Gate Welcome Center Vista Point
strings.d2.b0.tips: No bike? Take the number 28 bus to the bridge and walk across.
strings.d2.b1.name: Scoma's Sausalito
strings.d3.s0.name: Alcatraz Island
strings.d3.s0.tips: Ferry from Pier 33 (Alcatraz City Cruises, 45 USD). The cell house audio tour is narrated by former inmates. Book online weeks ahead; the first ferry is at 08:45.
strings.d3.s1.name: Pier 39 Sea Lions
strings.d3.s1.tips: Hundreds of sea lions on K-Dock. Touristy but fun.
strings.d3.s2.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
strings.d3.s2.tips: North Beach's world-champion pizza, near Washington Square.
strings.d3.s3.name: City Lights Bookstore
strings.d3.s3.tips: The Beat Generation bookshop (1953), next to Vesuvio bar.
strings.d3.s4.name: Coit Tower
strings.d3.s4.tips: A 1933 tower on Telegraph Hill with frescoes in the style of Diego Rivera's school. Take the lift for views, and look for parrots on the Filbert Steps.
strings.d3.b0.name: Mama's on Washington Square
strings.d3.b0.tips: North Beach brunch. Expect a queue.
strings.d3.b1.name: Musée Mécanique
strings.d3.b1.tips: Antique arcade machines at Pier 45. Free entry; an alternative to the sea lions.
strings.d4.s0.name: California Academy of Sciences
strings.d4.s0.tips: A living roof, rainforest dome, aquarium and planetarium in Golden Gate Park.
strings.d4.s1.name: Japanese Tea Garden
strings.d4.s1.tips: A tea garden from 1894 with a pagoda and bridge. Free early in the morning.
strings.d4.s2.name: Nopalito Haight
strings.d4.s2.tips: Sustainable Mexican food: carnitas, right by the park.
strings.d4.s3.name: Haight-Ashbury
strings.d4.s3.tips: The 1967 hippie corner, with Amoeba Music and vintage shops. Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies are 20 minutes away.
strings.d4.s4.name: Alamo Square Painted Ladies
strings.d4.s4.tips: Victorian houses against the skyline: the Full House shot.
strings.d4.b0.name: Zazie Cole Valley
strings.d4.b1.name: Conservatory of Flowers
strings.d4.b1.tips: A Victorian greenhouse; an alternative to the tea garden.
strings.d5.s0.name: Muir Woods National Monument
strings.d5.s0.tips: Coast redwoods up to 80 m tall. Park/shuttle reservation is REQUIRED (gomuirwoods.com). Allow 45 minutes by tour or car, and 1 hour for the main loop.
strings.d5.s1.name: Muir Beach Overlook
strings.d5.s1.tips: Views of the Pacific cliffs and a World War II lookout.
strings.d5.s2.name: Pelican Inn Muir Beach
strings.d5.s2.tips: An English pub with fish and chips and a fireplace.
strings.d5.s3.name: Mill Valley
strings.d5.s3.tips: A redwood town. Visit the Depot bookshop square.
strings.d5.s4.name: Marin Headlands Battery Spencer
strings.d5.s4.tips: The best postcard view of the Golden Gate. Hawk Hill, and fog rolling through.
strings.d5.b0.name: Stinson Beach
strings.d5.b0.tips: A long Pacific beach; in summer, an alternative to Mill Valley and the Headlands.
strings.d5.b1.name: Equator Coffees Mill Valley
strings.d6.s0.name: Tartine Bakery
strings.d6.s0.tips: Legendary sourdough and morning buns. Expect a queue at 08:00 on Guerrero; across the road is Mission Dolores, a church from 1776.
strings.d6.s1.name: Clarion Alley & Balmy Alley Murals
strings.d6.s1.tips: Latin street art, plus the Women's Building mural. A Precita Eyes tour is optional.
strings.d6.s2.name: La Taqueria Mission
strings.d6.s2.tips: An award-winning Mission burrito (no rice). Cash only, and a queue.
strings.d6.s3.name: Dolores Park
strings.d6.s3.tips: A hilltop park with city views. Bi-Rite ice cream (queue) in the sunny neighbourhood.
strings.d6.s4.name: Castro Street & Castro Theatre
strings.d6.s4.tips: The LGBT neighbourhood: rainbow crossing, Harvey Milk, and a 1922 cinema.
strings.d6.b0.name: Bi-Rite Creamery
strings.d6.b0.tips: Salted caramel ice cream, next to the park.
strings.d6.b1.name: Twin Peaks
strings.d6.b1.tips: A 280 m city panorama. Take the number 37 bus from Castro, and expect wind.
strings.d7.s0.name: Palace of Fine Arts
strings.d7.s0.tips: A 1915 imitation Roman ruin with a pond and swans.
strings.d7.s1.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
strings.d7.s1.tips: A new park with Golden Gate views and a playground, next to the Walt Disney Museum.
strings.d7.s2.name: Presidio Social Club
strings.d7.s2.tips: A restaurant in a former barracks. Brunch and a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: BART SFO
strings.d7.s3.tips: BART to the airport takes 30 minutes (from Embarcadero). Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
strings.d7.b0.tips: The Disney museum in the Presidio; an alternative to Tunnel Tops.
strings.d7.b1.name: Marina Green Breakfast Blue Barn
strings.note0: With Clipper (on your phone): Muni 2.75, cable car 9, BART SFO 10. The hills are steep; Muni Metro plus buses works well. Uber/Lyft/Waymo (driverless) also run.
strings.note1: SUMMER IS FOGGY: June to August brings morning fog and 15-18°C ('the coldest winter is a San Francisco summer'). Layer up; the bridge clears in the afternoon. September and October are the sunniest.
strings.note2: Book Alcatraz and Muir Woods weeks ahead. The Academy is 45 USD and Alcatraz 45. Tax of 8.6% and a 18-20% tip are not included in prices.
strings.note3: Try sourdough (Tartine, Boudin), Mission burrito, cioppino, dim sum and Ferry Building oysters; for coffee, Blue Bottle or Ritual.
strings.note4: Avoid the Tenderloin (west of Union Square) and SoMa around 6th Street at night. Never leave belongings in a car (window smashing). Homelessness is visible but the danger is low.
strings.note5: Follow Karl the Fog on Instagram; go to Twin Peaks or Battery Spencer at sunset to see the fog roll in.
strings.transit.name: Clipper Card
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on Muni, cable cars, BART and ferries; load it onto your phone
